name: BN6's support attack's end, a frame after its routine
subject: megaman
why: Each game's support family runs the chip's routine from the subfamilies' table (BN4 0x080EB9EA from 0x080220E0, BN6 0x080ED0DC from 0x0802CCB4, by bx r3). BN4's ends the attack in the same frame (bl 0x0800C9FC at 0x080EBA36, straight after the routine's result is stored); BN6's stores 1 in the attack's phase (movs r0,#1; strb r0,[r7,#1] at 0x080ED12A) and ends it the frame after, by that phase (ldrb r0,[r7,#1]; cmp r0,#0; bne at 0x080ED0DE to bl 0x08011714 at 0x080ED130). So on that one frame BN6's MegaMan still holds the support family (CurAction 0x15) with phase 1 where BN4's is back in his own state: his CurAction and the phase byte alone, there alone (tools/xdiff_bn4.py support_end). And from the next frame his own record of BN6's is a frame further behind BN4's than the battle is (megaman_clock: read that frame later, his object and AI data, what his state runner drives; his collision data and his object's visible bit, +0's 0x02, stay the battle's frame's, the status routines' by the collision data's timers: an invisibility's count and its blink, bn4_chip_invis; nothing else of the battle), until the world gives him a state (below). BN6's own support chips hold him so too: the engine's, not the chip's. bn4_chip_areagrab at t33, his records alike from t34 to t121 read so
